verses.text: In Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went together into the Jewish synagogue. They spoke so well that a large number of Jews and Greeks believed.
But the Jews who refused to believe stirred up the Gentiles and turned their minds against the believers.
So Paul and Barnabas stayed there a long time, speaking boldly for the Lord. The Lord showed that their message about his grace was true by letting them do signs and wonders.
The people of the city were divided. Some sided with the Jews, and others with the apostles.
Then some Gentiles and Jews, together with their leaders, made a plan to hurt them and kill them with stones.
But the apostles found out about it and escaped to Lystra and Derbe, cities in Lycaonia, and to the area around them.
There they kept on preaching the good news.
In Lystra there sat a man whose feet were crippled. He had been lame from birth and had never walked.
He listened as Paul was speaking. Paul looked straight at him and saw that he had faith to be healed.
So Paul called out loudly, "Stand up on your feet!" At that, the man jumped up and began to walk.
When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they shouted in the Lycaonian language, "The gods have come down to us in human form!"
They called Barnabas Zeus, and they called Paul Hermes, because he was the main speaker.
The priest of Zeus, whose temple was just outside the city, brought bulls and flowers to the city gates. He and the crowd wanted to offer sacrifices to the apostles.
But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard about this, they tore their clothes and rushed out into the crowd, shouting,

"Friends, why are you doing this? We are only human, just like you. We are bringing you good news, telling you to turn away from these useless things to the living God. He made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
In the past, he let all the nations go their own way.
But he has always given proof of who he is by the good things he does. He gives you rain from the sky and crops in their seasons. He gives you plenty of food and fills your hearts with joy."
Even with these words, they could hardly stop the crowd from offering sacrifices to them.
Then some Jews came from Antioch and Iconium and won the crowd over to their side. They threw stones at Paul and dragged him out of the city, thinking he was dead.
But after the followers had gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. The next day he and Barnabas left for Derbe.
They preached the good news in that city and made many followers. Then they went back to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch.
There they made the followers stronger and encouraged them to stay true to the faith. They said, "We must go through many hard times to enter God's Kingdom."
Paul and Barnabas chose elders for them in each church. With prayer and fasting, they put them in the care of the Lord, in whom they had put their trust.
After going through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
They preached the word in Perga and then went down to Attalia.
From Attalia they sailed back to Antioch. That was where they had been put into God's care for the work they had now finished.
When they arrived, they gathered the church together. They told everything God had done through them, and how he had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
And they stayed there with the followers for a long time.
